subject: Indexing patterns & cost targets — recap + next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@searchly.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Indexing patterns & cost targets — recap + next steps

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap so we have a shared view of the goals and next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Pain points you shared
- Relevance drift: current lexical + sparse signals miss recent user intent (esp. product names)
- Cost & latency: retrieval+rerank is increasingly the largest per-query expense; need predictability at scale
- Ops pain: nightly bulk rebuilds are brittle and cause uneven tail latency during catch-up windows

Current stack (as I understood it)
- Embeddings: in-house 768-d vectors
- Vector store: Qdrant for nearest-neighbor, Redis used for metadata cache
- Orchestration: nightly batch ingestion + streaming updates for user feedback

Scale / performance targets you gave
- Index size: ~600M vectors (you estimated ~600–750M; please confirm exact number below)
- Peak online QPS: 180–250 (search-heavy mornings & marketing campaigns)
- Typical write pattern: ~20k writes/day with a nightly bulk window (2–4AM UTC)
- Success criteria: end-to-end retrieval+rerank p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms; maintain cost < $0.02/query for the full pipeline

Proposed Redwood approach (high level)
1) Small perf PoC using a shard sample (10–20M vectors) to validate latency & recall tradeoffs.
2) Measure model + index config combos (flat quantized FAISS on GPU vs CPU sharded HNSW in Qdrant) and provide a per-qps cost/lantency estimate.
3) If PoC looks good, run a staged rollout with prefix caching and adjustable batching to smooth nightly rebuilds.

Immediate next steps (action items)
- Elena: confirm exact current index size (estimate above used 600M).
- Searchly: share a small sample export (5–10M vectors + 1k representative queries) to the shared Drive link below.
- Redwood (Ben): produce an initial qps/latency cost matrix and recommended config by EOD Thursday.

Attachments: searchly-index-stats.xlsx (we referenced the index numbers on the call)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-searchly-sample

Thanks — I’ll loop in Ben to scope the perf test and Monica for the mutual action plan.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-poc-outline.pdf (pdf)]
